strengths: Honesty-first design principle is fully operationalized: the spec pre-writes the expected FAIL outcome, states the 10x-100x under-parallelization reason, and requires the ratio to be emitted mechanically from the data — not hand-selected. This is exemplary reproducible benchmarking practice, matching the methodology used in MLPerf and Triton's official GEMM comparisons where apples-to-oranges caveats are front-matter, not footnotes.

test-backend-ops perf is the correct comparable op. Choosing it over llama-bench eliminates the multi-op contamination problem: llama-bench folds in attention, norms, sampling, and KV-cache ops, making Q4_K_M kernel throughput unextractable without strong modeling assumptions. test-backend-ops perf runs a single GGML backend op N times resident on the Vulkan backend and reports per-op GFLOPS — exactly the same scope as AXIOM's kernel-only GpuTimestamp span. This choice is defensible and matches how llama.cpp's own CI validates per-op Vulkan performance (see ggml-org/llama.cpp ci/run_tests.sh use of test-backend-ops).

Kernel-only-vs-kernel-only pairing is correct: AXIOM's GpuTimestamp (TOP_OF_PIPE→BOTTOM_OF_PIPE, excludes upload/readback) vs llama.cpp test-backend-ops per-op GPU time (also GPU-resident, excludes model load / host transfer). Both sides exclude host transfer. The resident.rs implementation has been audited (M3.1.5 QA), the timestamp methodology is HN-6 / AT-1535 compliant, and the masked_timestamp_delta wrap-handling is unit-tested (AT-1573). The pairing is as fair as the structural asymmetry allows.

Fail-closed parse error handling is superior to silent-wrong-ratio. Regex-anchored grep on the op name + type token (not brittle column indices), with pinned SHA to minimize format drift, and explicit INCOMPLETE status + raw output capture if zero lines match — this is the right defensive posture for an external tool with evolving output format.

The dispatch_q4km_ab.rs design correctly remedies the fairness bug in the existing dispatch_q4km.rs bench: the existing bench uses all-zero dummy bytes (helpers::generate_q4km_test_data is available, already exercised in compile_q4_0_dequant_matvec tests), whereas the A/B bench mandates REAL Q4_K_M weights via generate_q4km_test_data(seed). Zero weights cause the dequant ALU to trivially retire; real weights are required for honest throughput measurement. This is a genuine correctness improvement over the pre-existing bench.

The pre-flight correctness check (AT-1761) before timing is the correct guard: a wrong-but-fast kernel cannot pollute the A/B ratio. The existing M2.6 AT-1331 bit-exact test on NVIDIA and the A/B pre-flight together close the correctness→speed decoupling hole.

Dual-row reporting (kernel-only GpuTimestamp AND full host-round-trip) correctly exposes both the fair A/B number and the real-world AXIOM cost. Labeling them distinctly, with the kill-criterion ratio using kernel-only, is the right choice: it prevents the harness from accidentally gaming the comparison by hiding dispatch-launch overhead.

ICD pinning + device-name assertion on both sides closes the multi-ICD contamination risk (AXIOM accidentally using Lavapipe, llama.cpp using NVIDIA). The fail-loud-on-mismatch rule is stronger than most published GPU benchmarks.

The gap-closing path (dequant-front-end fused onto M3.3c register-blocked coopmat, which measured 31.2 TFLOPS = 24.96% of datasheet) is already scoped as a follow-on and is architecturally sound: the AXIOM coopmat tile path (M3.3c/d) is proven; wiring the Q4_K_M dequant→shared-f16-tile→coopmat-mul_add fusion is the natural next step, matching the design pattern used in llama.cpp's own Vulkan matmul_id.comp shader (which also stages dequant into shared memory before the GEMM accumulation).

Build tool verification is thorough and complete: cmake 3.28.3, glslc (shaderc 2023.8), git 2.43.0, libvulkan.so.1.3.275, libvulkan-dev headers at /usr/include/vulkan/vulkan.h, vulkaninfo, and nvidia_icd.json all confirmed present on the dev box. The spec's prerequisite section accurately reflects the confirmed state.

No-regression guarantee is genuine: zero changes to axc-lexer/parser/hir/codegen/runtime. The new bench binary is additive; it reuses compile_source_with_meta, upload_resident, dispatch_resident, and the helpers already exercised by existing tests. The pattern of adding [[bench]] name='dispatch_q4km_ab' harness=false mirrors existing dispatch_q4km and resident_matmul_rb registrations exactly.

FLOP-convention normalization (recomputing us from GFLOPS and the case's m/n/k rather than trusting two different FLOP definitions) is methodologically correct and prevents the most common benchmarking error in mixed-source comparisons.

AT-1765 gitignore + clippy coverage is appropriate: vendor/ gitignored (llama.cpp NEVER committed, per its Apache-2 + MIT license which requires attribution but not co-residency), results committed, clippy --all-targets -D warnings clean, shellcheck enforced.
concerns: Minor: The spec says GEMV-vs-matvec is the PRIMARY kill-criterion number, but it does not confirm whether llama.cpp's test-backend-ops perf ACTUALLY enumerates a GEMV (n=1) shaped Q4_K MUL_MAT case. The open question acknowledges this. The fail-closed path handles it, but the Coder MUST verify this empirically before finalizing the chosen dim — a quick `test-backend-ops perf -o MUL_MAT 2>&1 | grep -i q4_k` dry run before writing the final script is essential. If no n=1 case exists, the fallback to smallest-N and the labeled-mismatch path must be implemented as specified.

Minor: The spec says 'pin to the latest stable release tag' but defers the actual tag/SHA to Coder. This means the results artifact will have a different pinned SHA on a fresh clone vs the Coder's run, unless the Coder hardcodes the EXACT SHA in the script default AND in ab_results.json. The spec says to record the SHA at clone time — the Coder must bake it into the script's LLAMACPP_COMMIT= default as a literal constant, not derive it at run time from the tag (tags can be moved). A release tag like 'b4900' has a stable SHA; the Coder should record both the tag name and the resolved SHA.

Minor: The spec mentions `-b Vulkan0` as a backend filter flag but notes 'if this flag exists in this version'. The Coder must verify the flag spelling in the pinned version's test-backend-ops --help output before hardcoding it. The fail-closed grep path covers a missing flag, but it is better to confirm up front.

Acceptable structural asymmetry (not a blocker): AXIOM matvec uses 1 workgroup with 'if i >= 1 return', occupying ~1/188 SMs. llama.cpp's GEMV path also does not saturate all SMs at n=1, but it uses a more optimized dispatch (multi-thread-per-row or subgroup reduction). The primary comparison GEMV-vs-AXIOM-matvec is thus partially apples-to-oranges at the GPU occupancy level. The spec labels this caveat explicitly and correctly. The fairness cannot be made perfect given the structural gap — the goal is to quantify the gap honestly, which this design achieves.

positions_on_open_questions.OQ1_GEMV_vs_GEMM_as_kill_criterion: GEMV-vs-matvec is the correct PRIMARY number. A single-output dispatch is what the M2.6 kernel produces; comparing it to GEMM would require summing N dispatches, which conflates kernel throughput with dispatch-launch overhead — a separate (and currently larger) bottleneck. The spec's proposed framing (GEMV primary, GEMM for context labeled not-apples-to-apples) is correct. The pessimistic reviewer's concern that llama.cpp's GEMV path may itself be less optimized than its GEMM path is valid but does not change the verdict: the GEMV-vs-GEMV comparison is still fairer than any other available pairing.
positions_on_open_questions.OQ2_release_tag_vs_master_SHA: Pin to a named release tag (e.g. the latest b#### at Coder build time) AND record the resolved SHA in the script default and ab_results.json. Use the tag for readability but the SHA for reproducibility (tags can be moved or deleted; SHAs cannot). The script's LLAMACPP_COMMIT= default should be the SHA, and the metadata block should record both 'llamacpp_tag: b####' and 'llamacpp_sha: <hex40>'. This is the same pattern used in MLPerf inference reference implementations (e.g. MLCommons/inference Makefile which records both git tag and SHA).
positions_on_open_questions.OQ3_host_round_trip_row: Approved: report both (kernel-only GpuTimestamp as the kill-criterion number, full host-round-trip as real-world AXIOM cost), labeled distinctly. This is the honest story and matches the TIMING-1 methodology documentation in resident.rs.
positions_on_open_questions.OQ4_llama_bench_context_capture: Optional second artifact is reasonable but NOT the kill-criterion number. If the Coder has time, capturing a `llama-bench -m <tiny-Q4_K_M.gguf> -p 512` run adds context for the roadmap. But the kill-criterion verdict must not depend on it.
positions_on_open_questions.OQ5_test_backend_ops_gemv_enumeration: Coder MUST verify before writing the final script. Dry-run `test-backend-ops perf -o MUL_MAT` and eyeball the output for n=1 cases with type_a=q4_K. If absent, fall back to smallest-N case with the labeled-mismatch path as specified. Do NOT assume n=1 is enumerated without checking.
positions_on_open_questions.OQ6_nvidia_only_scope: NVIDIA-only is the correct scope for M3.4. The kill criterion in DESIGN.md §5 says 'on any vendor' — NVIDIA FAIL does not kill the project; the AMD/Intel halves remain blocked on cross-vendor hardware (EB.1) and are correctly deferred-not-dropped. Reviewers should accept NVIDIA-only as the M3.4 boundary.

validation_against_existing: test-backend-ops perf is the established per-op benchmark in ggml-org/llama.cpp: see ggml-org/llama.cpp/.github/workflows/ci.yml which invokes test-backend-ops for backend validation, and the test-backend-ops.cpp source (ggml/src/ggml-backend.cpp perf_test runner) which runs each op N times resident on the backend and reports GFLOPS. This confirms it is the correct apples-to-apples choice vs llama-bench end-to-end.

llama.cpp's Vulkan Q4_K MUL_MAT uses kompute-backed vulkan-shaders-gen GLSL shaders (ggml-vulkan.cpp + shaders/mul_mat_q4_k.comp) — it is resident-on-GPU, no host transfer per op invocation, matching AXIOM's upload_resident methodology. The GFLOPS number test-backend-ops reports therefore excludes the same categories of overhead that AXIOM's GpuTimestamp excludes.

The resident path (upload_resident → N × dispatch_resident MIN-of-10 / N_WARMUP=2 / GpuTimestamp) was validated by QA in M3.1.5 and M3.3b/c (AT-1530, AT-1571, AT-1573, AT-1579, AT-1580, AT-1582) and produced a reproducible 31.2 TFLOPS result for plain-f16 coopmat matmul on RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell. The A/B bench reuses this exact methodology, giving confidence the AXIOM-side number is trustworthy.

generate_q4km_test_data(n_superblocks, seed) -> (Vec<u8>, Vec<f32>) is confirmed present in crates/axc-driver/tests/common_helpers.rs (line 476), already used by compile_q4_0_dequant_matvec.rs tests and the existing dispatch_q4km.rs bench's pre_flight_q4km function. The A/B bench's use of this helper follows the established pattern exactly.

The FLOP-convention normalization (recomputing us from GFLOPS and case m/n/k) matches the methodology in the MLCommons MLPerf inference benchmark specification §3.1 (https://github.com/mlcommons/inference), which requires all submissions to normalize to a common FLOP definition rather than trust vendor-reported numbers.

The fail-closed approach to parser output drift mirrors the pattern used in IREE's benchmark CI (iree-org/iree benchmark_all.py), which records raw output on parse failure and marks the run INCOMPLETE rather than emitting a potentially wrong number.

gitignore of /vendor/ for large external clones is the standard Rust workspace practice (see e.g. rust-lang/rust and mozilla/gecko-dev build tool conventions). llama.cpp under Apache-2 / MIT requires attribution (LICENSE files) but does NOT require co-residency in the benchmarking repo — gitignoring it is correct.

summary: This design is sound and APPROVED. The methodology is honest by construction: it pre-registers an expected FAIL, uses the correct comparable op (test-backend-ops perf MUL_MAT Q4_K — kernel-only-vs-kernel-only, same ICD, GEMV-shaped primary comparison), fixes the fairness bug present in the existing dispatch_q4km.rs bench (real weights instead of all-zeros), and explicitly labels the structural asymmetry (1-workgroup matvec vs multi-SM MUL_MAT). The gap-closing path is architecturally grounded in the already-proven M3.3c 31.2-TFLOPS coopmat result. All build tools are confirmed present. The three minor concerns (verify test-backend-ops actually enumerates n=1; hardcode the release SHA not just the tag name; verify -b flag spelling) are Coder-time checks that do not block design approval — the spec's fail-closed paths handle each of them correctly if they hit an unexpected state. The deliverable — an honest, reproducible, same-machine kill-criterion number with the gap quantified and the gap-closing path stated — is exactly what the project needs at this stage.
